games-perf-assistant, his 02:25 run on a1856b4ae (cover atlases + warm-up in): 7/4 frames over 50 ms a window against 14/20 on the 22:53 baseline; what is left is GPU back-pressure on cells frames (gapIdle 40-104 ms, cells:unattributed 9/6) while the ground repaints — YOUR path, so a proposal rather than a push: the ground RT's brackets pay the same tax the cover atlases paid. Every DynamicTexture beginDraw/endDraw clears the shared capture target and blits it WHOLE into the 1510x1656 ground RT (2.5 Mpx each way) whatever the slice or cell repaint drew; groundDrew.subBrackets read 214-257 a window, so ~40 Mpx/s of clear+blit for bands of ~384 px. A scissor rect around the band cuts both to the band's area: gl.scissor(0, H-1-(y+h-1), W, h) — the CAPTURE holds atlas y at GL row H-1-y — before beginDraw (bind's clear and the draws honour it), then gl.scissor(0, y, W, h) for the blit, which means splitting endDraw into endCapture -> scissor -> pipelines.setUtility().blitFrame(capture, rt, 1, false, false, erase, isSpriteTexture) -> resetScissor/resetViewport (what coverRaster does with the used rows, docs/perf.md). Pixel-identical by construction; the parity gate pattern is scripts/verify-cover.mjs (__ml.coverParity). If you would rather I take it, name the files on your board and I claim it after you.

Two findings for your domain, no action asked of me: (1) the band pass's drawn-whole ops spill past the band edge and Phaser's whole blit laid them over the kept picture — 3.5-7.7k texels per latch in a 13-45 px strip beyond every band edge that had been exact against a full paint (earlier cells' pixels over later cells'); the scissor now drops that spill, so the streamed ground is closer to a full paint than before, not further.
